questions.question: Match each microbiological description to the correct stool pathogen. Pathogen options: Vibrio cholerae, Shigella sonnei, Salmonella typhimurium, Campylobacter, Aeromonas.
questions.question_raw: Stool pathogens, various microbiological features, match pathogen to features. Micro descriptions (4) and pathogens (5 – Vibrio, Shigella sonnei, Salmonella typhimurium, Campylobacter, Aeromonas)

parts.text: Micro 1 - microaerophilic, grows on charcoal-based selective media.
Micro 3 - non-lactose fermenter, catalase-negative, curved gram-negative bacillus.
Micro 4 - non-lactose fermenter, catalase-negative, biochemically inert.

parts_raw.text: Micro 1 - microaerophilic, grows on charcoal something something
Micro 3 - NLF, catalase negative curved GNB

questions.model_answer: a) Campylobacter (e.g. C. jejuni) - microaerophilic, grows on charcoal- or blood-based selective media (Skirrow/CCDA) at 42 degrees C. b) Salmonella typhimurium - H2S producing (black colonies on XLD/Hektoen/SS agar), non-lactose fermenter. c) Vibrio cholerae - non-lactose fermenter, comma/curved gram-negative rod, oxidase-positive facultative anaerobe growing on TCBS/alkaline peptone water. d) Shigella sonnei - non-lactose (or late-lactose) fermenting, non-motile, biochemically inert enteric. Aeromonas is the unused distractor.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the Vibrio descriptors (curved GNR, oxidase-positive, selective media) are in this chapter; the Campylobacter, Salmonella, and Shigella identifications rest on standard clinical microbiology (Mandell species chapters / Manual of Clinical Microbiology).

cohort_answer.text:
Campylobacter
Salmonella typhimurium
Vibrio
Shigella sonnei

questions.question: Practical station: a bench isolate is a gram-negative bacillus that is oxidase negative and catalase positive. Shown on blood agar, it is OF-glucose positive and DNase positive.
questions.question_raw: Practical station: BacT (Powerpoint) isolate - GNB, oxidase negative, catalase positive. Shown BAP, OF glucose positive, DNAase positive.

parts.text: Name 4 genera that are yellow-pigmented non-fermenters.

parts_raw.text: Name 4 genera that are yellow-pigmented non-fermenters.

questions.model_answer:
a) Stenotrophomonas maltophilia — among the clinically important aerobic gram-negative non-fermenters it is characteristically oxidase negative (a near-unique feature), catalase positive, DNase positive, oxidizes glucose/maltose, and forms lavender-green to yellowish colonies.
b) (1) Chryseobacterium (2) Elizabethkingia (3) Sphingomonas (4) Myroides (Sphingobacterium is also acceptable).
questions.beyond_mandell: The S. maltophilia identification (oxidase-negative, DNase-positive non-fermenter) rests on standard clinical microbiology/CLSI identification criteria; this organism is covered in its own Mandell chapter, not the slice read here.

questions.question: An Aeromonas hydrophila isolate has the following susceptibilities: ampicillin (R), ceftriaxone (R), aztreonam (R), meropenem (R), ertapenem (R), tigecycline (S).
questions.question_raw: Q61 (2018). Antibacterial Mechanism of Resistance. Aeromonas hydrophila organism with the following susceptibilities: Ampicillin (R), Ceftriaxone (R), Aztreonam (R), Meropenem (R), Ertapenem (R), Tigecycline (S)

parts.text: The organism possesses a carbapenemase that was inactivated by EDTA. Which class of carbapenemase is represented here?
Name one other gram-negative organism found in this same class of beta-lactamases.
Name two other (non-carbapenemase) mechanisms that can cause carbapenem resistance.

parts_raw.text: a) The organism possesses a carbapenemase which was inactivated by EDTA. Which class of carbapenems is represented here?
b) Name one other gram negative found in this same class of beta-lactamases
c) Name two other mechanisms (non-carbapenemase) that can cause carbapenem resistance?

questions.model_answer:
a) Ambler Class B metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL). EDTA chelates the active-site zinc, so inhibition by EDTA defines a zinc-dependent Class B enzyme; Aeromonas carries chromosomal CphA MBLs and acquired VIM/IMP-family MBLs.
b) Any one of: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (VIM/IMP), Klebsiella pneumoniae (NDM), Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (L1), Enterobacter cloacae, Escherichia coli (NDM).
c) (1) Loss or reduction of outer-membrane porins (e.g. OprD), decreasing drug entry. (2) Upregulation of efflux pumps (e.g. MexXY), often combined with an AmpC cephalosporinase or ESBL.
questions.beyond_mandell: The porin-loss and efflux mechanisms in part c are standard resistance concepts (CLSI/review literature); the Aeromonas slice names its MBLs but not these non-carbapenemase pathways.

cohort_answer.text: Ambler Class B: MBL. Other GNB in this class: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia (also E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter cloacae). Other mechanisms: decrease or loss of porin (OprD) and increased efflux pump (MexXY)

questions.question: What is the most likely organism in each of the following scenarios?
questions.question_raw: What is the most likely bug in the following scenarios?

parts.text: Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
Common variable immunodeficiency with bloating and diarrhea
Cancer patient with bullous skin lesions and a Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli

parts_raw.text: Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
CA patient with bullous skin lesions and Gram stain showing GPBs

questions.model_answer: a) Capnocytophaga canimorsus — a slender gram-negative rod with tapered ends inhabiting the canine oral cavity; classic cause of post-dog-bite sepsis, especially in asplenic, alcohol-abusing, or otherwise immunocompromised patients, and may progress to DIC and purpura fulminans. b) Aeromonas hydrophila — wound infection/cellulitis after fresh-water exposure (others to consider: Plesiomonas, Edwardsiella; salt water: Vibrio vulnificus, Shewanella; and Erysipelothrix from fish/animal handling). c) Giardia duodenalis (lamblia) — the classic cause of chronic bloating and diarrhea in common variable immunodeficiency. d) Clostridium septicum — atraumatic (spontaneous) myonecrosis with bullous skin lesions and gram-positive bacilli, strongly associated with underlying malignancy (colonic adenocarcinoma, hematologic malignancy/neutropenia).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only part (a) is covered in this chapter; (b) Aeromonas, (c) Giardia in CVID, and (d) Clostridium septicum/malignancy are established associations from their respective Mandell chapters, not the Capnocytophaga chapter.

cohort_answer.text: 1) Capnocytophaga canimorsus. 2) Aeromonas. Others: Burkholderia, Edwardsiella, Plesiomonas, Pseudomonas. Salt water: Vibrio, Shewanella, Erysipelothrix. 3) Giardia. 4) Clostridium septicum (w/o trauma), due to the malignancy

questions.question: What is the most likely organism to the species level in each of the following situations?
questions.question_raw: PM 14. What is the most likely organism to the species level in the following situations? AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB? (1); Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis (1); CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea (1); Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite (1)

parts.text: Acute myeloid leukemia with a central venous catheter and hemorrhagic bullae, gram-positive bacilli.
Fresh-water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis.
Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea.
Post-splenectomy patient who develops sepsis following a dog bite.

parts_raw.text: AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB?
Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis
CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea
Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite

questions.model_answer: a) Clostridium septicum (spontaneous non-traumatic gas gangrene with hemorrhagic bullae in neutropenic/malignancy hosts, associated with colorectal cancer). b) Aeromonas hydrophila (fresh-water necrotizing soft-tissue infection). c) Giardia duodenalis (lamblia) - classic chronic diarrhea in CVID. d) Capnocytophaga canimorsus - splenectomy is a strong risk factor for this dog-bite pathogen.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the dog-bite organism (Capnocytophaga canimorsus) is from this chapter; Clostridium septicum, Aeromonas hydrophila, and Giardia are established associations from general Mandell/ID knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: Clostridium septicum (in immunocompromised can cause gas gangrene without trauma, differentiating from C. perfringens; translocates from GI to hematogenous spread to skin; associated with colorectal CA). Aeromonas hydrophila (fresh water). Giardia lamblia/duodenalis. Capnocytophaga canimorsus.
